label: prop:sw-period-residue-sum
title: The Seiberg–Witten period is an algebraic residue sum
html:
Proposition. The Seiberg–Witten period is an algebraic residue sum

Let \mathcal{S}_c \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) be the exceptional divisor at a branch point z_c (Bring's surface smoothness). Let \lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)} be the n-th prolonged Seiberg--Witten differential of the MI--SW abelianisation, a meromorphic 1-form with poles only at the branch points. Let \gamma be a cycle enclosing a subset E of those poles. Then

\oint_{\gamma}\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)}
\;=\;
2\pi i \sum_{p\,\in\,E}\mathrm{Res}_p\,\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)}.

The enclosed set E is part of the claim, not a bookkeeping detail (corrected 2026-08-29, bean qou-6v5l). This statement previously ranged the sum over all p \in \mathcal{S}_c and justified it as "the residue theorem on the compact Riemann surface". That is backwards: on a compact surface the residue theorem says the residues of a meromorphic 1-form sum to zero, so summing over every pole would force a_D^{(n)} = 0 at every jet level — see QOU.Brings.period_eq_zero_of_total_residue_vanishes. Relatedly, \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) has H_1 = 0 and so has no generating cycle for a period to be taken over; only a bounding cycle has a residue-sum value at all. Identifying E was recorded here as the open geometric content the keystone conj:sw-prolongation-period-eq-mean-qdim still needs.

E is not identifiable, because under the classical-jet rule there is nothing to enclose (2026-09-03, bean qou-qx7j). Every residue vanishes individually, so every subset gives period zero and the choice of E carries no information. The reason is local and needs neither a global primitive nor the compact surface: writing z = z_c + t^2 at a simple branch point, d/dz = (1/2t)\,d/dt acts on Laurent coefficients as f \mapsto \bigl(e \mapsto (e+2)f(e+2)\bigr) — the operator ddz that QOU.Brings.RamificationParityMonodromy already defines for this exact setting — and at the residue slot e = -2 its multiplier is (-2)+2 = 0. The t^{-2} coefficient of a z-derivative is always zero, because the only input that could reach it is the constant term and differentiating a constant kills it (QOU.Brings.ColourCubicBranchLocus.ddz_residue_slot_eq_zero).

The branch locus is also bar-symmetric, which excludes the natural contour. \Delta's coefficient list [16,24,35,50,35,24,16] is palindromic, so z^6\Delta(1/z) = \Delta(z) and the locus is invariant under the Hecke bar-involution z \mapsto 1/z. Reducing by w = z + 1/z gives 16w^3 + 24w^2 - 13w + 2, whose discriminant -80000 < 0 leaves one real root, located in (-2,-1) by C(-2) = -4 < 0 < 23 = C(-1); and a real w with |w| < 2 gives |z| = 1 exactly. So the six branch points split 2+4: two bar-fixed points lying on the unit circle, and one bar-orbit of four with reciprocal moduli. The unit circle is therefore not an admissible contour — it passes through two branch points, and it is the candidate the \oint_{\mathcal{S}_c} notation above suggests.

So the open problem is upstream of E: which prolongation. The q-difference prolongation is untouched by this, as it is by prop:sw-classical-jet-exactness.

Subject to that, once E is fixed the prolonged Seiberg--Witten period a_D^{(n)} = \oint_{\gamma}\lambda_{\mathrm{SW}}^{(n)} functions as an algebraic residue sum: it is evaluated by collecting the local residues at the poles in E, with no contour integration beyond identifying which poles \gamma encloses.

Residue support and body order. The branch-point poles support the residues. The n-th prolongation lifts the connection to the n-jet bundle J^n E, so the weight data of rank n grades the residue family at level n; the residue sum therefore carries the body-order grading, and the period at vertical degree n yields the n-body contribution. Each residue constitutes a per-block quantum-dimensional weight on the Wedderburn decomposition restricted to that level.

What the grading cannot be (added 2026-08-29, bean qou-6v5l). It is not a one-to-one indexing of the level-n residues by the blocks \lambda \vdash n, and the vertical degree n does not increase the number of poles. The pole locus is the branch locus of the colour cubic, and that is exactly 6 points independent of n — its discriminant \mathrm{disc}_X = -16z^6 - 24z^5 - 35z^4 - 50z^3 - 35z^2 - 24z - 16 is squarefree, with three conjugate pairs at |z| \approx 0.943,\, 1.000,\, 1.061. A bijection onto the blocks would need p(n) \leq 6, which fails from n = 5 (p(5) = 7, p(6) = 11, p(n) \to \infty). What grows with n is the pole order, X^{(n)} \sim (z - z_k)^{1/2 - n}, not the number of poles. This bounds the indexing, not the equality a_D^{(n)} = \mathrm{lw}(n-1): six residues may of course sum to what eleven quantum dimensions sum to.
